label: 2026 Q3 (Jul–Sep)
asOf: after-hours price of $293.65 on 28 Oct 2026 (7:25 pm ET, StockAnalysis)
headline: Cloud revenue doubled, but what it earns no longer covers the spending: data centers are now funded by stock and debt

points.b: Cloud is the only part accelerating
points.t: Google Cloud +103% y/y, 62% of the company's added revenue; the release singled out TPU system sales as a significant source.
Revenue +25%, yet operating income fell $0.19B quarter on quarter: depreciation +49% and unallocated AI research +71%.
$85.2B of bonds, $42.9B of new common stock and $19.1B of convertible preferred this year, zero buybacks; future purchase commitments have reached $924B.

reaction: Stock: closed at $324.89 (+1.3%) on report day; results came after the close and the stock fell to $293.65 (−9.6%) after hours. Three reasons: EPS of $2.12 was far below the $3.02 expected, and still only $2.67 excluding the paper loss on its SpaceX stake; 2026 capex stayed at $195–205B while 2027 was again said to “increase significantly”; and the CFO warned Q4 cloud margins will be pressured by renting third-party compute. The next day it closed at $283.82 (−12.6%), extending the after-hours drop. Two revenue estimates: Reuters $128.2B, Investing.com $127.2B.

segments.title: By business
segments.take: Of the $25.2B of added revenue, cloud was 62%. Advertising still grows steadily, but only cloud is accelerating.

rows.why: Includes GCP AI compute and AI solutions, Workspace, and TPU systems sold into customers' own data centers. Operating income $11.1B, a 36.2% margin versus 23.7% a year ago.
Management said search query growth was the highest in five years, with AI driving queries including commercial ones. Growth slowed from Q2's 17%.
More than 150M YouTube Music and Premium subscriptions (including trials), Google One, Play and devices.
Growth slowed from 13% in Q2 to 9%, below the expected $11.34B.
Ads on third-party sites and apps, essentially not growing.

segments.note: Shares are of total revenue ($127.58B); “other” includes Other Bets ($0.37B) and hedging changes. Google Services totaled $96.30B, +10.6% y/y, with a 40.7% operating margin.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Google holds four roles in this chain at once: it pays to build data centers, sells compute and TPUs, rents others' compute and invests in AI companies. This quarter shows clearly for the first time that the paying role now depends on outside money.

items.w: Q3 capex of $51.4B was 121% of operating cash flow of $42.3B, versus 49% a year ago. About 65% is servers and networking (6-year depreciation) and 35% data centers. The full-year guide implies another $63–73B in Q4.

This year: $85.2B of bonds, $42.9B of new common stock ($27.6B left in the ATM program) and $19.1B of 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred; long-term debt rose from $46.5B to $125.1B, and buybacks stopped. Future purchase commitments are $924B, with another $152B of leases not yet commenced.

Cloud backlog grew from $514B to $561B, about 55% recognized within 24 months. TPU customers include Anthropic (direct, and via Broadcom), Apple, Citadel Securities and nearly 100 others; TPU systems are also distributed through Crux AI (a joint venture with Blackstone) and Oracle. Blackstone and large banks are lining up $63B for Anthropic to lease Broadcom chips, money that also flows back into this chain.

Short of supply, Google began renting third-party compute as a “bridge” at the end of Q3, with more in Q4; the CFO said this will weigh on cloud margins near term. TPU systems are built ahead (only for signed contracts), so inventory rose from $2.4B to $13.3B: cash goes out first and revenue comes later.

Non-marketable equity investments rose from $68.7B to $135.2B in nine months, with only $24.2B of new purchases; it also holds $90.4B of marketable equity. This quarter's $8.7B loss came mainly from a drop in SpaceX's valuation, which pushed GAAP EPS far below expectations.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Google's future rests on cloud and TPUs: the backlog covers more than two years of recognition, and TPUs are starting to be sold as full systems like NVIDIA's. The variables are how much capex this revenue takes and how much more outside money it needs.

items.w: Cloud backlog rose $47B in a quarter, about 55% recognized within 24 months; 18 product lines each exceed $1B of annual revenue. But supply is short, so it began renting third-party “bridge” compute at the end of Q3.
Up 12.5 points in a year; renting third-party compute in Q4 will pressure margins near term, the CFO warned. Depreciation +49% and unallocated AI research +71% absorbed most of the added revenue.

TPU systems are sold directly to Anthropic, Apple, Citadel and others, and distributed through Crux AI (a Blackstone JV) and Oracle; they “ramp meaningfully” in 2027. Inventory rose from $2.4B to $13.3B for it.
Query growth is the highest in five years, but AI Mode still monetizes below classic search; Q4 growth will be a few points lower again.
Only that 2027 capex will “increase significantly”, with the number in Q4; the CFO now argues with “return on capital over the investment cycle above the cost of capital” rather than free cash flow.

Free cash flow over the past year was only $19.7B, with $147.2B raised externally this year. Watch whether cloud backlog keeps growing, whether TPU inventory turns into cash, Q4 capex of $63–73B and the 2027 guide, and whether stock and bond issuance continues.

extras.title: Why profit didn't keep up
extras.take: Revenue was $7.8B higher than in Q2, yet operating income fell $0.19B; the extra revenue was largely absorbed by three costs.

items.w: Depreciation of property and equipment was $8.37B, versus $5.61B a year ago. Data centers built over the past two years are being depreciated, and capex is still accelerating.

“Alphabet-level” costs are mainly the people and compute for training general models like Gemini: −$4.5B a year ago, up 71%. The CFO said depreciation and data-center operating costs such as energy will keep growing.
R&D expense of $20.6B; 205,000 employees versus 190,000 a year ago.

trends.why: Cloud margin up 12.5 points in a year
More than doubled in a year; the Q4 guide is higher still

valuation.take: At the after-hours price, the GAAP P/E is about 15x, but on profits inflated by about $129B of investment gains; on operating income it is about 29x, and the forward P/E is about 22x, right at its five-year median. The real issue is cash: a market cap of about $3.6T against only $19.7B of free cash flow over the past year, a 0.5% yield. Today's price is a bet that this capex will pay back.

forward.title: Full-year cash flow from the capex guide
forward.sub: no profit guidance, so we look at cash
steps: Free cash flow in the first three quarters: $10.1B − $5.9B − $9.1B = −$4.8B
Q4 capex = full-year guide of $195–205B − $132B spent = $63–73B
Q4 operating cash flow at the three-quarter average of about $42.4B
→ Q4 free cash flow about −$21B to −$31B, full year about −$25B to −$35B
The company says 2027 capex will “increase significantly”, so the cash gap still needs financing
forward.note: Our estimate from company guidance, not a company forecast. Operating cash flow is held flat; in reality it moves with profit and working capital.

cash.title: Capex eats all the cash
cash.note: Operating cash flow was also held back by building TPU systems ahead (inventory up $10.9B in nine months) and paying a $5.2B 2018 EU fine. Cash is actually $138.3B higher than at the start of the year because financing proceeds sit on the balance sheet first. The CFO said returns on capital over the investment cycle will be “well above the cost of capital”, but admitted free cash flow will be lower.

scenarios.note: Bear: all cloud and search growth is eaten by depreciation, energy and rented compute; base: cloud margin stays above 30% with low-double-digit search growth; bull: TPU system sales take off. EPS = operating income × (1 − 19%) ÷ 12.37B shares; P/E at the 29 Oct close of $283.82. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: 2027 EPS × our P/E; price at the 29 Oct close
pricezone.why: Down 13% after the report, the price is still above the zone: buying now, the base case gains only about 4% while the bear case loses about 27%. At the zone midpoint of about $238 the reward/risk is about 1.9; the $215 low end is close to the bear-case price. The 20–27x multiples sit around its five-year median forward P/E of about 22x; no higher, because cash flow now depends on outside financing.

changes.before: For a decade, data centers were built from its own cash flow while buying back about $60B a year.
changes.now: $147.2B of bonds, stock and preferred this year, buybacks stopped; the CFO now argues with “return on capital over the investment cycle” rather than free cash flow.

changes.before: In Q2: supply can't keep up with demand; plans to bring in third-party “bridge” compute.
changes.now: Third-party compute only came online at the end of Q3, with more in Q4, and near-term cloud margin pressure flagged.

changes.before: Q2 first confirmed TPU system sales revenue, mostly in 2027.
changes.now: Nearly 100 customers, naming Anthropic, Apple and Citadel; TPU systems sold together with Crux AI (Blackstone JV) and Oracle; Pichai called it an “important platform”.
+12%: FX, the EU ending the small-parcel duty exemption hit APAC e-commerce advertisers, World Cup timing, and AI Mode still monetizes below classic search; Q4 a few points lower again.

items: Annualized revenue has reached $500B; search query growth is the highest in five years
Cloud backlog of $561B, about 55% recognized within 24 months; 18 product lines each above $1B of annual revenue
1B Gemini app users; the model API processes nearly 32B tokens a minute, 4x a year ago
TPUs built only for signed contracts; placing them in customer and third-party facilities means building fewer of its own data centers
